title: Kew Riverside Primary School — Parent-led evidence and action, maintained by Yann Stoneman

records.title: Ofsted: school continues to be Good

records.title: Ofsted inspection: full July 2026 report (school-hosted)
records.summary: Strong standard in early years, inclusion, and personal development and wellbeing; Expected standard in achievement, curriculum and teaching, and leadership and governance. Attendance and behaviour Needs attention: persistent absence is the concern, while behaviour is praised. Safeguarding Standards met. Next steps include attendance and consistent teaching approaches. These are category judgements, not a single overall grade.
records.locator: 16-page report for URN 133343. 8 July 2026 is the inspection date; publication date not inferred. School-hosted copy linked from its Ofsted page. Judgements: PDF pages 1–5; next steps and pupil leadership/younger readers: page 6; attainment: pages 9–10. Central index still lists 2021 latest on 22 September 2026.

records.title: School Place Planning Strategy: the Kew area
records.summary: The Kew section expected longer-term demand from housing to fill available capacity. It discussed a continued temporary reduction at Darell. It also noted that the private finance initiative could complicate expansion at Kew Riverside Primary School. Housing figures and forecasts are assumptions from 2023, not current permissions or actual pupil numbers.
records.locator: March 2023 strategy; printed page 37, planning area 7. Read assumptions against subsequent updates.

rankingMethod: One immediate official-response action plus seven optional ways to help. Rank records display order, not probabilities or a required sequence. The seven options retain their previous relative order, based on decision relevance, potential evidence strength and usefulness before a decision. School-specific feasibility remains unproven. Crowdfunding follows the costed recovery plan because they are connected, not because feasibility or success is established. Enrolment follows demand testing and must be developed with the school and tested against a recovery budget.

approaches.title: Respond to the council
approaches.effort: Give your own views; preparing a recovery plan is optional.
approaches.why: A short case with sources is easier to assess than a count of signatures alone. Agree who covers budgets, demand, alternatives and the effects on pupils, while keeping each person's own views.
approaches.next: Respond through the official council-linked form by its stated date, 16 October 2026. Keep a copy, check later committee agendas and respond again during any statutory representation period.
approaches.limits: A petition can get an issue considered, but it is not a veto. Public campaigning does not replace a response during the formal representation period.

approaches.title: Help build a plan to keep teaching at Kew
approaches.effort: Share one budget question, a public example or your own skills in finance or education.
approaches.evidence: Needs school-specific budgets and partner commitments
approaches.why: A credible alternative gives decision-makers a choice they could put into practice. Model a smaller intake, shared leadership, a federation or suitable use of spare space, with a realistic plan for staff and funding.
approaches.next: Draw up a three-year budget with low, central and high pupil scenarios. Name who would deliver it and what support they would commit.
approaches.limits: A federation or merger may preserve teaching on the site without preserving the current institution. Agree which outcome matters. No option is demonstrated viable by the records collected here.

approaches.title: See if fundraising could help
approaches.effort: Share one funding question, a public example or your own fundraising experience.
approaches.evidence: Needs a recovery budget, donor interest and an agreed recipient
approaches.why: Could local residents, families and businesses help fund a viable future for Kew Riverside Primary School? Money raised locally could help fund a costed recovery plan and give the school time to make changes.
approaches.next: Work out the funding needed for an agreed recovery period. Find an organisation able to receive and manage the money. Ask the school and council for a written assessment of how a funded plan would affect the proposal. Check how interested donors are before deciding whether to launch a public appeal.
approaches.limits: A one-off donation does not fix a shortfall that continues each year. Fundraising would need a credible plan for pupil demand, costs and future income. Local wealth does not mean donors have committed. Raising money would not by itself secure a decision to keep the school open.
approaches.forecast: The council projects an accumulated budget deficit of over £400,000 by 2028/29. This is a forecast, not an agreed fundraising target.
approaches.stage: Ideas and feasibility only; no campaign, donations or pledges.
approaches.feedbackPrivacy: Private human review; no publication or automatic forwarding.

questions.question: What funding would actually be needed, and for how long?
questions.help: Public budgets, an explanation of annual versus accumulated deficits, or financial modelling experience.
questions.prompt: the funding needed and the recovery period

questions.question: Would a funded recovery plan change the council’s proposal?
questions.help: Published decision criteria or statements could help. This needs an answer from the school and council; visitor opinion alone cannot settle it.
questions.prompt: how the school and council would assess a funded plan

questions.question: How could the school become sustainable after the initial funding?
questions.help: Costed ideas for shared leadership, use of space, income or realistic pupil recruitment, with assumptions and drawbacks.
questions.prompt: making the school sustainable after initial funding

questions.question: Who could receive and manage the money?
questions.help: Relevant experience with a school, PTA or suitable charity. No organisation has been agreed as a recipient.
questions.prompt: who could receive and manage contributions

questions.question: How could a campaign reach beyond current parents?
questions.help: Inclusive outreach, public grants, business partnerships or examples of matched giving. Please leave out donor names and private contact details.

questions.question: Are there comparable school rescue campaigns to learn from?
questions.help: Public links, amounts raised, what happened to the school in the end and lessons about sustainability.
questions.prompt: lessons from comparable school rescue campaigns

questions.question: What would make a future appeal credible?
questions.help: Financial reporting, milestones, surplus funds and what should happen if a target is missed or closure proceeds.
questions.prompt: conditions and accountability for a future appeal

questions.question: What expertise could help assess or organise this?
questions.help: Your own budgeting, fundraising or administration experience. An offer of help does not commit you.
questions.prompt: expertise that could help assess this option

approaches.title: Check the pupil-number forecast
approaches.effort: Share one dated public source, or a question about pupil numbers or local housing.
approaches.evidence: School and local forecasts published; assumptions need scrutiny
approaches.why: The borough trend is clear, but a borough average cannot settle the case for one school. Compare forecasts with actual admissions, local cohorts and dated housing-delivery assumptions.
approaches.next: Test the published school and Kew-area forecasts against their inputs and past errors. Reconcile dated housing assumptions and examine credible delivery scenarios.
approaches.limits: A historic forecast is not proof that a later forecast is wrong. Proposed homes do not automatically become pupils at Kew Riverside Primary School.

approaches.title: Help more families find the school
approaches.effort: Suggest one local group or place where the school could share verified information.
approaches.evidence: Needs available places, school coordination and a recovery budget
approaches.why: Help local families find the school through nurseries, parent groups, community notices, word of mouth and social media. Give them verified school information and a direct way to ask about a visit. Check any lasting rise in enrolment against a costed recovery plan.
approaches.next: Agree a time-limited recruitment pilot with the school; establish available year groups, previous recruitment results, owners and costs. Seek a school/council assessment of what sustained increase, by when, would change the recovery plan.
approaches.limits: Viral reach is not guaranteed. Views, enquiries and applications do not establish enrolments or viability. No agreed pupil target guarantees continued operation. Normal admissions arrangements and the closure proposal remain relevant.
approaches.stage: Editorial proposal to develop with the school; no campaign accounts or endorsement implied.

approaches.title: Check what closing would really save
approaches.effort: Share a public cost figure or ask which costs would continue after closure.
approaches.evidence: PFI arrangement documented; closure cost model missing
approaches.why: The useful comparison is the avoidable cost of keeping the school open against the full cost of closing it. Continuing building payments could change the balance.
approaches.next: Ask for a year-by-year cash-flow comparison. Include PFI obligations, transition costs, redundancy, transport and any income from using the site. Separate costs that end from costs that continue.
approaches.limits: The existence of a PFI contract does not prove that closure saves nothing. Its terms and the council's actual options must be established.

approaches.title: Show what a move would mean for children
approaches.effort: Suggest one question about support, safe journeys, siblings or available places.
approaches.evidence: Transition commitments published; detailed impact evidence still sought
approaches.why: Decision-makers need practical evidence about each year group, extra support, safe journeys, accessibility, continuity and siblings. A total of empty places does not answer every family’s questions.
approaches.next: Request capacity by year group and provision for special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Send anonymised, specific examples, with realistic ways to reduce the impact, and alternatives.
approaches.limits: Evidence of the impact on children may improve a transition plan without preventing closure. Keep children's identities and each child's needs out of public campaign material.

approaches.title: Flag a possible legal problem
approaches.effort: Point to a specific document or process concern. Seek specialist advice promptly about any legal deadline.
approaches.evidence: Depends on the actual proposal and decision record
approaches.why: An education or public-law solicitor can assess a specific concern about the process, evidence or legal duties. They can do this once the relevant documents are available.
approaches.next: Share the notice, consultation papers, decision report and an exact timeline. Ask quickly about the deadlines and remedies that apply.
approaches.limits: Disagreement with the merits is not by itself a legal defect. Parents do not have a general direct right of appeal to the Schools Adjudicator for a community-school closure. This ranking is not legal advice.
